# Tickets

All work happens on a ticket, and every ticket ends with evidence. This skill is the single source of truth for the ticket format, the states, and the evidence rule.

## Where tickets live

Read `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` first. It names the tracker:

- **local** (default): `tickets/<feature>/NN-<slug>.md`, one file per ticket, plus `tickets/<feature>/spec.md`. Ticket ID is `<feature>/NN`.
- **github**: GitHub Issues through `gh`. Ticket ID is `#<number>`. Status is a label, blockers use native blocking links or a `Blocked by` section, the progress log is issue comments.
- **other**: follow the paragraph in that file.

`tickets/BOARD.md` is a generated one-page summary. Read it before opening individual tickets. Regenerate it with `node .ai/cli/bin/cli.mjs status --write` after any status change.

## Local ticket format

```markdown
# NN: <Title>

**Type:** design | dev | automation | review | qa | doc-drift | bug | release
**Status:** <state>
**Blocked by:** None | NN, NN
**Owner:** <name>

## What to build
End-to-end behaviour from the user's point of view. No file paths.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: ...
- [ ] AC2: ...

## Inputs
- Links to docs/inputs, spec, ADRs, designs this ticket relies on.

## Evidence
- Commits:
- PR:
- Tests:
- Review:
- Docs updated:

## Progress log
### YYYY-MM-DD <who>
- Did: ...
- Next: ...
```

## States

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `needs-triage` | Raw, not evaluated yet |
| `needs-info` | Waiting on someone for information |
| `ready-for-agent` | Fully specified, an agent can take it |
| `ready-for-human` | Needs a human (judgement, access, or the loop gave up) |
| `in-progress` | Claimed and being worked |
| `in-review` | Built, checks green, waiting for review |
| `done` | Merged into the project's working branch (`branch show`; the main line when none is set) and evidence recorded |
| `wontfix` | Will not be done; say why in the log |

A ticket is **blocked** when any ticket in `Blocked by` is not `done`. The **frontier** is every `ready-for-agent` ticket that is not blocked, lowest number first.

## Acceptance criteria IDs

Number every criterion `AC1`, `AC2`, ... and never renumber. Tests and manual cases reference them as `<ticket ID>#AC<n>` (`cart/01#AC2`). `trace` uses these IDs to prove coverage. Criteria without an explicit `ACn:` prefix are numbered by position, which breaks when reordered, so always write the prefix.

## Bug tickets

`Type: bug` tickets also carry `**Severity:** S1 | S2 | S3 | S4`, `**Found in:**` and, when raised while working another ticket, `**Found during:** <ticket>`. Use the `report-bug` skill to file them. Open S1 and S2 bugs block `gate release`.

## Who owns which type

design → architect · dev, bug → builder · automation → sdet · qa → qa · review → reviewer · doc-drift → builder · release → whoever cuts it (`/cut-release`)

## Request with no ticket

When the user describes a change and asks to implement it, but no ticket covers it, do not start. Say: "This needs a ticket first so the change is recorded."

1. Draft the ticket from their words: feature folder, title, `Type`, 2 to 5 numbered criteria (`AC1`...), and a one-line "What to build". Reuse an existing feature folder when it fits; otherwise pick a short kebab-case one.
2. Show it and ask for a go-ahead. Their yes covers the criteria.
3. Write `tickets/<feature>/NN-slug.md` (next free number), set `in-progress`, add the first progress log entry quoting the request, then continue with `implement`.

This works with or without `grill-with-docs` → `to-spec` → `to-tickets`. Never write code before the ticket exists. Trivial housekeeping may use `[no-ticket]`.

## Requirements change mid-ticket

When the user changes their mind while a ticket is `in-progress`, change that ticket, not a new one and not the code alone:

1. Edit the ticket first: add, reword or drop criteria. Never renumber; mark a dropped one `- [ ] ~~AC2: ...~~ dropped: <reason>`, and give a new one the next `ACn`.
2. Log a `Requirement change` entry in the progress log: date, what changed, why, what was dropped.
3. Then change the code and tests to match. Re-run the criterion tests that were affected.
4. If the change is a different job (a new feature, not a reshaping of this one), say so and create a separate ticket; if it contradicts an ADR, update or supersede the ADR (`domain-modeling`).

The ticket then reads as the full history of what was asked and why it ended up as it did.

## Rules

1. **Claim before work.** Set `in-progress`, add a progress log entry, save, then start.
2. **Log every session.** Two to five lines: what was done, what is next, any decision made (link the ADR).
3. **Reference the ticket in every commit** (`<feature>/NN` or `#123`). CI rejects commits without one; use `[no-ticket]` only for trivial housekeeping.
4. **Evidence before done.** For code tickets, `gate deliver --ticket <id>` must pass before `in-review`: every criterion ticked and named by an automated test, Commits and Tests recorded. Fill every Evidence line that applies: commit SHAs, PR link, test command and result, review findings, docs updated. A `done` ticket with empty evidence fails `validate`.
5. **Never delete tickets.** Use `wontfix` with a reason.
6. Tick acceptance criteria as they are met, not at the end.
